sweepers.text: You're locked into Again Radio. Twenty-four hours of a life in progress. Turn the sound up.
Shout to all the heads locked in worldwide right now. Wherever you're listening, you're in the right place.
Late night frequencies on Again Radio. This one's for anyone still awake and thinking.
Reconnecting to the live room. Right back on the pulse.

intro.text: Delilah Montagu singing straight out of her kitchen into an iPhone memo. Fred caught the feeling while waiting on his laundry. Hold tight... here it comes.

outro.text: Delilah, pulling us all out of this. Unbelievable energy.

intro.text: Danielle Balbuena, 070 Shake on the vocal. That raw acoustic emotion wrapped in pure club euphoria.

outro.text: Danielle, smile on my face. That smile is now permanent.

intro.text: The very first breath of the Actual Life journey. Nathan's words, caught in transit, reminding us all to just keep going.

outro.text: Nathan, still breathing. The heartbeat of the archive.

intro.text: Kammy Purcell on the vocal. Fred pitched down her acapella from an Instagram video while riding the Eurostar. Pure warmth.
Tanya. Only on the record does the name get a second half. Turn this one up.
Pangbourne crew in full effect. Skrillex, Flowdan, and Fred. Four years in the making. Watch the low end on this drop.

outro.text: Flowdan and Skrillex with Fred. Heavyweight pressure.

intro.text: Written during those legendary countryside sessions with Skrillex and Four Tet. Turn the lights out for this one.
Future, Swedish House Mafia, and Fred. Studio sound welded to the rave.
Dense, relentless energy. Fred wrote this to break the sound system. Here we go.
Obongjayar's voice arrives and the whole track opens up. Dedicated to his sister. Beautiful feeling right here.
The final chapter of the Boiler Room. The night is dark and the name is Clara.
Built from something fragile. Romy and Fred letting the chords hold the entire room.

boiler-room-london.text: Stepping into the iconic London Boiler Room. Sweat on the walls, pure electricity.

rooftop-naples.text: Heading over to Naples on that sun-drenched terrace. Golden hour over the sea.

times-square.text: Times Square, New York City. A yellow school bus and three friends stopping traffic.

tiny-desk.text: NPR Tiny Desk. No backing tracks, just classical piano, marimba, and live MPC loops.

facts.text: Fred knocked on Brian Eno's door at sixteen and joined his acapella group. Eno mentored him for over a decade before they made Secret Life together.
Every name in Fred's titles is a real person he met. The voice notes on his phone become the emotional soul of the music.
Before releasing solo records, Fred produced massive chart-toppers for Ed Sheeran, George Ezra, and Stormzy on his laptop.
During the 2022 Boiler Room, a dancer bumped the CDJ stop button. Fred just grinned, hit play, and turned it into the defining moment of the set.
